_comment: THE TOP MENU, for both apps (docs/design/navigation.md, sections 3 and 13; rung 1 built 2026-11-03). Infinite-of-X: a category or a page in it is a row here, never code.

Read by the desktop app (src/gui/navigation.rs: once at start and again when this file is saved, never each frame; a copy is built into the exe for a data folder without it) and by the website through scripts/gen-navigation.js, which writes the website's part into web/shared/shell.js (a test fails while that is out of date: run `node scripts/gen-navigation.js` after editing this file or a word it names).

categories: the design's eight, in order, each a page of its own; `items` are the category's other pages (the secondary row of rung 2). Every entry has an `id` (unique in this file), `label` and `hint` (keys in data/i18n/en.json), `icon` (a name in web/shared/icons.js; `humanity` is the brand H; the desktop app draws the icon of the entry's page, src/gui/widgets/icons.rs `nav_icon`, until rung 2 draws these names), `page` (the desktop page: an id src/gui/dispatch.rs `page_id` gives, `none` for the world, or null when the desktop has no page for it yet), an optional `section` (the part of that page it opens: a side-list section today, such as the Dev page's `claude`; on the world, `picker` is the character picker), and `web` (the website address, or null when the website has no page for it). A category also has `colour`, a theme token (data/gui/theme.ron). An item may say `desktop_only` (no website page by nature; the website will show it dimmed and open /download), `web_only`, and `new` (a page this design adds and has not built yet; where `page` or `web` is set on a new entry, it opens what does that job today, and `_note` says what).

THE OWN-LIFE CATEGORY'S NAME IS OPEN (section 16.1, question 1: "Home" clashes with the player homes; "Life" is recommended). Its id is the neutral `own_life` and its words are the key `nav.own_life`, so renaming it is one word in data/i18n/en.json.

outside: what a person can reach that the design's two rows leave out, each with `why` (the title screen, an alias, the website's own pages). A test holds every desktop page and every website page to exactly one place in this file (categories, items or outside): none lost, none twice.

today_row: what the single top row shows UNTIL rung 2 draws the two rows (the brief: where today's row and the design disagree, today's row wins). `desktop` is src/gui/pages/escape_menu.rs's groups (a theme token each, a dot between groups); `web` is web/shared/shell.js's (a CSS class each, a divider between); `web_active` maps an entry to the older key the website lights its tab by, where the two differ (the pages' data-active and shell.js's address list).

items.label: nav.mission
items._note: On the desktop the Mission Dashboard is the Humanity page's first section today; the website's /mission forwards to the Library's mission essay until it becomes the desktop page's mirror (section 8).

items.label: nav.people
items._note: People is new on both apps (section 8, rung 7). Until it is built, both open the Directory (the desktop's Identity page, the website's /identity), which becomes its Look someone up part.

items.label: nav.rules
items._note: New on the desktop (section 9); the website has it.

items.label: nav.roadmap
items._note: New on the desktop (section 9); the website has it.

items.label: nav.devlog
items._note: New on the desktop (section 9); the website has it.

categories.label: nav.play
categories._note: The world, with the character and world played last (or the picker when none is recorded). No game runs in a browser, so the website's Play opens /download. Section 16.1, question 2: a tap will open Play's own page and a press and hold will go into the world (rung 2).

items.label: nav.servers
items._note: Servers is new on both apps (section 8, rung 7). Until it is built, the desktop's opens the servers you run (the Relay Control page, today opened from the chat's sidebar), which becomes its Yours part.

categories.label: nav.own_life
categories._note: Its name is open (see the comment at the top). Its page today is the Home page (your homestead).

items.label: nav.ops
items._note: Its desktop twin is the Servers page's Yours part (section 9).

items.label: nav.widgets
items._note: On the desktop the widget test bench is a part of Settings (Settings > Widgets).

items.label: nav.server_settings
items._note: The website's /admin holds the ADMIN part only (section 9, a gap); the chat's cog still opens the desktop page too.

outside.why: The title screen, shown at launch; never in a menu (section 3).
An alias: this page id forwards to the Profile page (`real`), which the own-life row's Profile opens (src/gui/pages/real.rs).
The website's front door: shell.js draws it itself at the row's left end (section 3: it becomes the site's name).

outside.label: nav.onboarding
outside.why: The learn-by-doing chains; Start here on the front door opens it (section 9). Today's website row shows it where the desktop shows Quests.
The Library's Accord shelf on a permalink of its own, an address to share (section 9).
The community dashboard, to be merged into Mission (section 9).
The Wallet's help page, to move into the help system on both apps (section 9).
Recovery through trusted people: a part of Settings > Account on the desktop (section 9).
The printed card's QR address, never in a menu (section 9).
